q: Computer generations are mainly identified by major changes in which of the following?
explain: A generation is a broad stage of technological development, mainly marked by major changes in processing hardware.

q: Which technology was the basis of the first generation of computers?
explain: First-generation computers used vacuum tubes for electronic switching and amplification.

q: Smaller size, lower power use and better reliability helped which device replace vacuum tubes?
explain: The transistor is a semiconductor switch and amplifier that was smaller, cooler and more reliable than a tube.

q: VLSI stands for:
explain: VLSI is Very Large-Scale Integration, in which very large numbers of transistors are placed on one chip.

q: In the textbook convention, the second generation of computers (transistors) covers which period?
explain: The textbook ranges are 1940-1956, 1957-1963, 1964-1971, then microprocessors and AI emphasis.

q: Integrated circuits characterise which generation of computers, with the textbook period 1964-1971?
explain: ICs mark the third generation, which is dated 1964-1971 in the textbook convention.

q: Which statement about the date ranges of computer generations is correct?
options: New technology instantly replaced older machines
Every textbook uses exactly the same dates
They are textbook ranges with overlapping boundaries
explain: The ranges are textbook conventions. Newer technology did not instantly replace older machines, so boundaries overlap.

q: Approximately how many vacuum tubes did ENIAC contain?
explain: ENIAC contained approximately 18,000 vacuum tubes.

q: Which of the following was electromechanical rather than a vacuum-tube electronic computer?
explain: Harvard Mark I was electromechanical. ENIAC, UNIVAC I and IBM 701 were vacuum-tube machines.

q: Which machine used a magnetic drum as its main memory?
explain: The first-generation IBM 650 used a magnetic drum as main memory.

q: Which of the following is an example of a second-generation computer?
explain: IBM 7094 is a listed second-generation machine, along with IBM 1620, CDC 1604 and CDC 3600. ENIAC and IBM 701 are first generation.

q: Jobs are collected and run with little user interaction during execution. This describes:
explain: Batch processing runs collected jobs with little interaction. It was important in the second generation, but is not exclusive to it.

q: Which pair of languages became established during the second generation?
explain: Assembly language was important in the second generation, and FORTRAN and COBOL also became established.

q: Which development became increasingly important in the third generation?
explain: Third-generation systems used ICs and relied increasingly on multiprogramming and time-sharing, with keyboards and display terminals for interactive use.

q: Which of the following is commonly listed as a third-generation example?
explain: IBM System/360 and System/370 and the ICL 2900 are commonly listed third-generation examples, although many System/360 models used hybrid Solid Logic Technology modules.

q: What does PDP stand for in the DEC PDP family of computers?
explain: PDP is Programmed Data Processor, a family that spanned different technological periods.

q: Which was introduced in November 1971 and is widely recognised as the first commercially available single-chip microprocessor?
explain: Intel 4004 was the first commercially available single-chip microprocessor. Pentium 4 and AMD Athlon are much later processor families.

q: Which of the following characterised fourth-generation computers?
options: Vacuum tubes and punched cards only
Microprocessors and VLSI supporting compact, affordable personal computers
explain: In the fourth generation the CPU moved onto an integrated circuit and VLSI density made personal computers affordable.

q: Which of the following is a vector supercomputer rather than a personal computer?
explain: The Cray X-MP was a vector supercomputer, while the others are personal computers.

q: Which of the following is an emphasis of fifth-generation computing?
explain: The fifth generation emphasises AI, expert systems, knowledge-based systems, neural networks, NLP, parallel processing and intelligent robotics.

q: In which year did Japan's formal fifth-generation computer project begin?
explain: Japan's project began in 1982 and combined knowledge information processing, large-scale parallel processing and logic programming.

q: Which statement about KIPS is correct?
options: It stands for Knowledge Information Processing System and describes a processing approach
It is a type of storage disc
explain: KIPS is Knowledge Information Processing System, a processing approach and not an input/output device.

q: Which of the following is a better description of what defines a fifth-generation computer?
options: Emphasis on AI, knowledge processing and parallel processing
explain: Processor families (Pentium 4, AMD Athlon) and device categories (smartphone, tablet) do not define a generation; the AI and knowledge-processing emphasis does.

q: Which memory type was widely used as main memory in the transistor era?
explain: Magnetic-core main memory was widely used in the second generation. Delay lines and electrostatic storage belong to the early electronic era.

q: HVD stands for:
explain: HVD is the Holographic Versatile Disc, a specialised holographic optical-storage format.

q: Which statement about SSDs is correct?
options: They are exclusive to the fifth generation
They are Solid-State Drives, a form of flash storage, and are not exclusive to the fifth generation
They store data on magnetic tape
explain: SSD means Solid-State Drive and most SSDs use flash storage. They are not exclusive to the fifth generation.

q: A historical class of computer smaller and less expensive than mainframes, many of which supported multiple users, is called a:
explain: Minicomputers sat between mainframes and personal computers in size and cost, and many supported multiple users.

q: Which language is designed for scientific and numerical programming and became established in 1957?
explain: FORTRAN is used for scientific and numerical programming. COBOL is for business data processing.

q: Which of the following correctly lists time units from LONGEST to SHORTEST?
explain: A millisecond is 1/1,000 s, a microsecond 1/1,000,000 s, a nanosecond 1/1,000,000,000 s, and a picosecond 10^-12 s.

q: The language named from 'Matrix Laboratory', used for numerical computation, is:
explain: MATLAB takes its name from Matrix Laboratory. Lisp is List Processing and Prolog is Programming in Logic.

q: In operating-system development, which approach divides processing time among tasks or users to give interactive service?
explain: Time-sharing splits processing time among users or tasks for interactive use. Batch jobs run with little interaction.

q: Which of the following gives the correct broad order of network development?
explain: Networks grew from standalone systems to LANs, WANs, the Internet and cloud computing, and the older kinds remain in use.

q: Which device provides both input and output?
explain: A touchscreen displays output and accepts touch input.

q: In quantum computing, a qubit can be prepared in:
options: A superposition of the states associated with 0 and 1
explain: A qubit can be in a superposition of 0 and 1, but measuring it gives one result, 0 or 1.

q: Which of the following is an example of natural language processing (NLP)?
explain: Voice assistants, chatbots, translators and spam filters all analyse human language.

q: Which statement about the 'sixth generation' of computers is correct?
options: It has a universally accepted definition and start date
It is an informal label some textbooks use for quantum computing, nanotechnology and IoT, with no universal definition
It began in 1982 with Japan's project
It means computers using vacuum tubes
explain: There is no universally accepted sixth-generation definition or starting date; the label is informal.

q: Which machine ran the first program stored in electronic memory on 21 June 1948?
explain: The Manchester Baby (Small-Scale Experimental Machine) ran the first stored program. EDSAC followed in 1949 as an early practical stored-program service.

q: Which two people are recognised as co-inventors of the integrated circuit?
explain: Jack Kilby demonstrated a working semiconductor circuit in 1958, and Robert Noyce developed the practical monolithic silicon IC concept in 1959.

q: Herman Hollerith's punched-card tabulation was used for which event?
explain: Hollerith developed punched-card statistical tabulation for the 1890 US Census. Punched-card control existed earlier on Jacquard looms.

q: EDSAC stands for:
explain: EDSAC is Electronic Delay Storage Automatic Calculator. The first option is EDVAC, the second ENIAC and the third UNIVAC.
